items.title: Agents - OpenCode
items.snippet: Agents are specialized AI assistants that can be configured for specific tasks and workflows. They allow you to create focused tools with custom prompts, models, and tool access. The plan agent can be used to analyze code and review suggestions without making any code changes.

items.title: Researchers open autonomous robotics learning to the world | Stanford Report
items.snippet: A free online textbook, video lectures, and hands-on resources are making cutting-edge autonomy knowledge accessible to developers, researchers, and robot enthusiasts everywhere. Principles of Robot Autonomy (PoRA) is a new textbook inspired by a course series taught at Stanford since 2017. PoRA aims to bridge the divide, bringing classical robotics and modern AI together in a unified framework.

items.title: Adaptive agentic intelligence framework using Strands Agents
items.snippet: The Adaptive Agentic Intelligence Framework (AAIF), built with Strands Agents, utilizes small language models (SLMs) to handle routine tasks locally, rather than routing all requests to a single large, expensive model. This approach aims to reduce API costs and maintain low latency for local operations. It builds on research suggesting SLMs are sufficiently powerful and economical for many agentic system invocations.

dropped.title: Multimodal Embodied Agents: A Unified Capability-centric Perspective from Computer-Use to Robot-Use
dropped.snippet: Multimodal agents (MMAs) sustain interaction through reasoning, memory, tools, and feedback, most visibly as computer-use agents, while robotic systems (RSs) couple sensing and actuation under physical dynamics. We define multimodal embodied agents (MMEAs) as goal-directed systems that couple multimodal task reasoning with physical action and revise decisions from the resulting feedback. This paper raises a central question: what changes when a multimodal agent moves from computer-use to robot-use?

dropped.title: NVIDIA Advances Isaac Platform for General-Purpose Robotics With New Reference Humanoid, Frameworks, Simulation Pipelines and Data
dropped.snippet: NVIDIA today announced a major expansion of the NVIDIA Isaac™ open robotics development platform, adding a reference humanoid, datasets and runtime, along with updates to its robot learning framework. These technologies provide developers an integrated path from data to deployment to bring general-purpose robots to the real-world faster. Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA, stated that general-purpose robotics is advancing at extraordinary speed, with the 'ChatGPT moment for robotics' fast approaching.
